staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, so all line references below are anchored to this exact source snapshot.

classification.classification_note: The saved ASan sink is the second `plist_free()` of a node that `plist_from_openstep()` already freed while attempting its OpenStep-'strings' fallback parse. The project bug is the stale out-parameter alias that survives the fallback parse failure.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 54949 (libplist): heap-use-after-free READ 8 in `plist_free_node -> plist_free -> oplist_fuzzer`.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 224-byte witness starts with a `// ...` comment line, then a quoted string token `"Some UTF-1153#84014360082783957 string\\bs"` immediately followed by ` = (` and a one-element array literal, and later a malformed top-level entry whose bytes begin `22 4b 9e 22 2c` (`"K\\x9e",`). `node_from_openstep()` skips the comment, parses only that first quoted string, and returns a heap `plist` node in `*plist` while leaving `ctx.pos` on the trailing `=`. `plist_from_openstep()` interprets that `=` as OpenStep 'strings' syntax, frees the initial node, resets `ctx.pos` to the start of the buffer, and retries with `parse_dict_data()`. The retry successfully consumes the first dictionary item, but the next quoted token `"K\\x9e"` is followed by `,` instead of `=`, so `parse_dict_data()` sets `ctx.err`. Vulnerable code then frees the retry dictionary `pl` and returns `PLIST_ERR_PARSE` without clearing or overwriting `*plist`, so the out-parameter still aliases the node freed earlier. `oplist_fuzzer.cc` ignores the parse error and unconditionally calls `plist_free(root_node)`, and `plist_free_node()` immediately reads `node->parent` from the freed 48-byte `node_t`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ. The fix resolves this exact path by inserting `*plist = NULL;` immediately after the first `plist_free(*plist)`.

source.description: Source and first lifetime-materialization step. After skipping the leading comment line, `node_from_openstep()` parses the next quoted token as a standalone `PLIST_STRING` and stores the resulting heap node in `*plist`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 224-byte file `gt_results/arvo_54949/poc` with SHA-256 `f99c17dff11fc77ca912b105c26bff97fe92694a80a935b681dc6ecf8c39c66c`. Its relevant verified structure is: a leading `// ...` comment line, then the quoted token `"Some UTF-1153#84014360082783957 string\\bs"` followed by ` = (`; later bytes begin a malformed retry item with `22 4b 9e 22 2c` (`"K\\x9e",`).
source.note: This is the first scored project statement after the unscored fuzz harness boundary. The allocated node is the same object later freed at `plist_from_openstep():853` and reread at `plist_free_node():331`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Allocation origin for the 48-byte `node_t` that backs the initial parsed string node. AddressSanitizer's allocation stack points here via `plist_new_node()` and `node_from_openstep()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: This allocation occurs when step 1 materializes the first non-comment quoted token from the staged witness into a heap `plist` node.
tainted_value_origin.note: The object allocated here is later freed through `plist_from_openstep():853` and then reread by the second `plist_free()` call.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The fallback-to-'strings' branch invalidates the initial parsed node before storing any replacement or nulling the out-parameter, so `*plist` becomes a dangling alias if the retry parse later fails.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch adds `*plist = NULL;` immediately after this statement. That change is sufficient because the later retry path only assigns `*plist = pl` on success.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The second `plist_free()` enters `plist_free_node()` with the dangling `node_t *`, and evaluating `node->parent` for `node_detach()` reads the freed object.
sink.note: The saved ASan report is `heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` at `src/plist.c:331`, with stack `plist_free_node -> plist_free -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

parser_admitted.description: After the first parse returns a standalone node, the parser explicitly admits the OpenStep-'strings' fallback path because the next unread byte is `=`. The stale-pointer bug only occurs on this fallback branch.

evidence_limitations: No `trace_feedback.json` was present, and `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation, so this trace is entirely source-grounded from the staged vulnerable checkout, the staged PoC bytes, and the saved ASan report.

Stage 01 captured the final second-free AddressSanitizer stack, not parser-internal breadcrumbs. The exact retry failure on `"K\x9e",` is derived from the staged PoC bytes and the only matching `parse_dict_data()` error branch at `src/oplist.c:544-547`.

coarse_trace.summary: The parser skips the leading comment line, parses the next quoted token as a standalone string node, and leaves `ctx.pos` at the trailing `=` delimiter.
`plist_from_openstep()` interprets that `=` as strings-data syntax, frees the initial node, and retries the whole buffer as a dictionary-like strings file.

The retry parse accepts the first dictionary item but then hits a malformed key/value separator on the later `"K\x9e",` entry, frees the retry dictionary, and returns parse error without clearing the stale output pointer.
The harness unconditionally frees the returned `root_node`; `plist_free_node()` immediately dereferences the already-freed node and reproduces the saved heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: Source/allocation step. `node_from_openstep()` skips the leading `// ...` comment line, parses the next quoted token `"Some UTF-1153#84014360082783957 string\\bs"` as a standalone `PLIST_STRING`, and allocates a heap node for it. When control returns to `plist_from_openstep()`, `*plist` points to that node and `ctx.pos` is parked on the following `=` byte.

Because step 1 stopped before an `=` delimiter, `plist_from_openstep()` treats the buffer as candidate OpenStep 'strings' data and takes the fallback branch instead of returning the standalone string node.

Root-cause invalidation step. The initial heap node from step 1 is destroyed before any replacement value is stored in the out-parameter, so `*plist` becomes a dangling alias. The fix inserts `*plist = NULL;` immediately after this free.

The fallback parse restarts from the buffer start and successfully consumes the first dictionary item `"Some UTF-1153#84014360082783957 string\\bs" = ( ... );`. On the next item, the bytes `22 4b 9e 22 2c` (`"K\\x9e",`) parse as a key but the following delimiter is `,` instead of `=`, so this branch marks the retry parse as failed.

Because step 4 set `ctx.err`, `plist_from_openstep()` frees the retry dictionary `pl` and returns parse error. The success assignment `*plist = pl` at line 862 is skipped, so the output pointer still equals the freed node from step 3.

The harness ignores `plist_from_openstep()`'s error return and unconditionally frees `root_node`. Since step 5 never replaced or nulled the out-parameter, `root_node` still carries the dangling pointer from step 3.

Sink. The second `plist_free()` enters `plist_free_node()` with the dangling pointer from step 6. Evaluating `node->parent` for `node_detach()` reads the freed 48-byte `node_t`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` at `src/plist.c:331`.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack flows through `plist_new_node()` into `node_from_openstep():792`, where the first non-comment quoted token is materialized as the heap node later freed twice.

free_context.note: ASan's previous-free stack identifies the first `plist_free(*plist)` in the strings-fallback branch as the invalidation point for the node later reread by the harness's unconditional cleanup.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The allocation and previous-free stacks both refer to the same `node_t` created for the first parsed string token. The logical bug is the later `plist_from_openstep():853` invalidation that leaves the out-parameter aliasing that freed node when the retry parse fails.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved ASan stack is `plist_free_node (src/plist.c:331) -> plist_free (src/plist.c:449) -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput (fuzz/oplist_fuzzer.cc:29)`, and the fine trace refines the earlier in-function path inside `plist_from_openstep()` that frees the initial node and returns the stale pointer before the observed second free.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 3 frees the node stored in `*plist`, step 5 returns without replacing or nulling that out-parameter, step 6 passes the same stale pointer back into `plist_free()`, and step 7 immediately rereads the freed node in `node_detach(node->parent, node)`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_54949 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/oplist_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` with stack `plist_free_node -> plist_free -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: OpenStep plist strings-fallback witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 224-byte file with SHA-256 `f99c17dff11fc77ca912b105c26bff97fe92694a80a935b681dc6ecf8c39c66c`. Its relevant verified structure is: a leading `// ...` comment line; then the quoted token `"Some UTF-1153#84014360082783957 string\\bs"` immediately followed by ` = (` so the first parse stops with `ctx.pos` on `=` and enters the strings-data fallback; later, during the retry parse, a subsequent quoted token begins with bytes `22 4b 9e 22 2c` (`"K\\x9e",`) so `parse_dict_data()` sees `,` instead of `=` and fails. Stage 01 proves only this exact witness and the observed fallback-failure path; this contract does not generalize to other malformed OpenStep files.
